title: Burning and Suppression of Solids
platform: International Space Station, Microgravity Science Glovebox
summary: BASS (Burning and Suppression of Solids) burned thin and thick solid fuels (fabrics, films, PMMA slabs/spheres, candles) in a small flow tunnel inside the ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox, varying airflow speed (and later O2) to map flame spread, growth and extinction without buoyant flow. It showed that some fuels burn in microgravity where they would not in normal gravity (e.g. opposed-flow spread), and that concurrent-flow flames quench near 1 cm/s. Points come from two results presentations, not from a per-run table; links to run numbers are inferred.

tests.notes: 1 and 2 cm wide, 8.5 cm long sheet; area density 18 mg/cm2. Quote: "decreasing concurrent flow speed to a very low value (around 1 cm/s), quenching extinction was observed" (ASGSR slide 33; same in overview slide 26). Slide gives no run number, O2 or pressure for the quenching event, so derived_from is [] (no evidence ties specific runs). O2 21% and 1 atm remain assumed (ISS cabin nominal); no run-level statement exists. ISS cabin O2 varied between runs (overview slide 30: 21% to 22%), so confidence for O2 is low. The red dashed 'Concurrent-Flow Extinction' marker on the spread-rate plot is an extrapolation line, not a measured point. Open: No evidence of which runs quenched or of the O2/pressure at that event; o2_status and pressure_status stay assumed. BASS-II quenching runs (psi25 Table 7.1) were at 17-19% O2 and must not be used for this 2012 point.

normal_gravity_reference.note: slide 31: 1-g with flow (10 cm/s): growing flame size and spread; concave base, extended soot zone (0-g: steady flame size and spread). Slide wording: "Growing flame size and spread".

tests.notes: 2 cm wide sheet. Spread rate stated on slide 29: "Concurrent and Opposed Spread at ~ 10 cm/s 2.55 mm/s versus 1.21 mm/s" (fit VF=0.20U+0.56 gives 2.56). Run ids (not in derived_from, per contract): most probably CSV Test 7 (GMT 96, 4/5/2012, SIBAL 2 cm), which the BASS-II report lists as GMT96-T7, 2.2 cm, 10 cm/s, 21% O2, 'BASS' (Table 7.1 p.96); match is by width/flow/date, not stated on the slides. O2 21% and 1 atm come from the BASS-II report (sec 7.1.4: the four BASS-series SIBAL tests are all 21 percent O2; sec 7.1.3: ambient pressure was 1 atm), not from the PSI-26 slides. Outcome: BASS-II report p.95 describes the 2.2 cm, 10 cm/s, 21% O2 flame as decaying until complete burnout (about 40 s); the ASGSR slides do not state fuel fate. Open: O2, pressure and outcome rest on a secondary source (BASS-II report, a different investigation) tied to this point by width/flow match; the ASGSR slide 20/38 run (ignition at 10 then reduced to 5 cm/s) might be a different run than Test 7 (fixed 10 cm/s).

2 cm wide sheet. Spread rate ~1.57 mm/s read from the plotted 2 cm concurrent point at 5 cm/s (overview slide 25; fit VF=0.20U+0.56 gives 1.56); not given as text. ASGSR slides 20-21/38 show ignition at 10 cm/s then flow reduced to 5 cm/s. Run ids (not in derived_from, per contract): probably CSV Test 8 (GMT 96, 4/5/2012, SIBAL 2 cm) = GMT96-T8 in BASS-II report Table 7.1 (2.2 cm, 5 cm/s, 21% O2, 'BASS'); match by width/flow/date only. O2 21% and 1 atm from the BASS-II report (sec 7.1.4 and 7.1.3), not from the PSI-26 slides. Outcome: BASS-II report p.95 says the 5 cm/s flame took more than 60 s to burn the whole sample; the PSI-26 slides do not state fuel fate. Open: Spread rate is plot-read (not stated). Run tie (Test 8) is by width/flow match; the slide's 10-to-5 cm/s run may be another run, so O2/pressure/outcome are secondary-source inferences.

1 cm wide sheet. Flame-tip speed from slide 23 fit xtip = 1.71 t + 2.25 (base fit xbase = 1.68 t - 13.81); flame reaches steady state after ~10 s. Slides label the run '10 cm/s'; the plotted 1 cm concurrent points sit at ~11 and ~19 cm/s. Run id (not in derived_from, per contract): CSV Test 10 (GMT 131, 5/10/2012, SIBAL 1 cm) = GMT131-T10, 1.2 cm, 11 cm/s, 21% O2 in BASS-II report Table 7.1; CSV Test 11 (GMT 222) is the 19 cm/s point, not this one, so it is not linked. O2 21% and 1 atm from the BASS-II report (sec 7.1.4 and 7.1.3), not from the PSI-26 slides. Outcome partial_burn = flame sustained at steady state; fuel fate not stated anywhere. Open: Flow is 10 cm/s on slides but 11 cm/s in the BASS-II table and plot; outcome (fuel fate) not stated by any source, partial_burn is an enum approximation.

normal_gravity_reference.note: Downward flame spread (opposed flow) in 1-g with this material is not possible in normal air (flame self-extinguishes)

tests.notes: 2 cm wide sheet. 1.21 mm/s is the opposed value stated at '~10 cm/s' on slide 29; the opposed plot (slide 30) shows ~1.43 mm/s at 10 cm/s and ~1.2 mm/s at ~9 cm/s, so the stated 1.21 may belong to the ~9 cm/s points. Outcome complete_burn confirmed by slide 25: "Flame quickly reaches steady state and goes out when it runs out of fuel." Run id (not in derived_from, per contract): the only SIBAL row marked opposed in the CSV is Test 5b (GMT 181, 6/29/2012), but it may be the 90 s stepped run (slide 26) rather than this constant 10 cm/s sequence, so the link is unproven. O2 21% and 1 atm assumed (ISS cabin nominal); no PSI-26 statement or BASS-II table row covers opposed runs. Normal-gravity reference (slide 25 note, slide 33): downward (opposed) spread is not possible in normal air. Open: Spread value 1.21 vs plot ~1.43 at exactly 10 cm/s; O2 and pressure remain assumed; run id unproven. Test 5b shares GMT 181 with Ultem Test 16 (ISS atmosphere 21-22%) but that is context, not a statement for SIBAL.

2 cm wide sheet. Slide 26: flow decreased in discrete steps from 10 cm/s to about 1 cm/s, total burn time 90 s; flame persisted through the steps, no opposed extinction stated. Lowest opposed plotted point is ~1.4 cm/s, ~0.62 mm/s (slide 30); spread_rate left null because the plotted point is at 1.4, not 1 cm/s. Outcome partial_burn is an approximation (flame sustained; end state at 1 cm/s not stated; 85 mm sample over 90 s is consistent with full consumption but this is inference). Run id (not in derived_from, per contract): likely CSV Test 5b (GMT 181, 6/29/2012, 'SIBAL 2 cm opposed flow'), the only opposed SIBAL row. O2 21% and 1 atm assumed (ISS cabin nominal). Open: Outcome could be complete_burn (burn time ~ sample length / mean spread rate) but no source says so; O2 and pressure assumed; run tie is by CSV label only.

Slide title says 14 cm/s, body text says 15 cm/s; 14 kept as the title condition. Candidate run ids (not in derived_from, per contract): CSV 'Nomex III Natural' Test 14 (6/28/2012) and 'nomex natural III' Test 15 (7/19/2012); the slide gives no test number or date. 15 mm initial diameter sphere Flame persists at <1 cm/s flow, even when a nitrogen jet is imposed; extinguished only at zero flow (low-flow quenching floor not resolved below 1 cm/s). Quote: "after a series of flow reductions, the flame goes out when the flow speed is zero".

1 cm wide flat sheet. Slide 54: flame ~1 cm, persisted a very long time; went out only when the air flow was shut off (fuel not exhausted), so partial_burn. 'In air' is explicit but no O2 percentage is given; 21% assumed (the 21-22% ISS-atmosphere statement on slide 30 is for Ultem/Nomex runs only). Pressure not stated; 1 atm assumed. Air flow direction on the slide is right to left in the image; the montage shows only the flame (no sample), so concurrent vs opposed cannot be determined. CSV 'PMMA 1 cm' runs exist in 2012 (Tests 30-33) and 2013 (Tests 26-28, when O2 was varied), so the run cannot be tied and derived_from stays []. Quote: "burning in air at low flow speed (around 9 cm/s)". Open: O2 and pressure remain assumed; flow direction relative to spread unknown; run not identifiable (2012 vs 2013 candidates).

tests.material: Paraffin wax candle in ceramic tube
tests.notes: Paraffin wax candle in ceramic tube, 17% O2, flow up. Slide 59: flame at <1 cm/s, test concluded when flow turned off and flame goes out. Slide 60 (candle sequence, same family): 17% O2/N2, 1 atm, flow stepped 5,4,3,2,1,<1 cm/s. derived_from set to [] because no slide gives run numbers, and CSV candle Tests 82/82a/82b are dated 7/3/2012, before the O2-variation tests the overview calls 'more recent' (slide 4); 17% candle runs are more likely the 2013 candle rows (e.g. Tests 85, 89, 93, 95), also unproven. Quote: "test is concluded when the flow is turned off and the flame rapidly goes out". Open: Whether slide 59 and slide 60 show the same test (pressure cited from slide 60) is not stated; source runs unknown; zero-flow quench is the only limit stated.
